name: Sorafenib
route_note: oral tablets twice daily without food

discovery.note: A bi-aryl urea found by screening for RAF1 (CRAF) kinase inhibitors; anti-angiogenic VEGFR/PDGFR activity proved clinically more important.

tagline: First systemic therapy to extend survival in advanced liver cancer
summary: Sorafenib is an oral multi-kinase inhibitor that blocks RAF kinases and the VEGF and PDGF receptors, inhibiting tumour cell signalling and angiogenesis. It is approved for advanced renal cell carcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma and radioactive-iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer; in 2007 it became the first drug to prolong survival in advanced liver cancer.
mechanism: Sorafenib binds the inactive (DFG-out) conformation of several kinases. Inhibition of VEGFR2/3 and PDGFRβ reduces tumour angiogenesis, while inhibition of CRAF and BRAF reduces MAPK signalling in tumour cells.
It also inhibits KIT, FLT3 and RET. Its activity in hepatocellular carcinoma is thought to be mainly anti-angiogenic.

history.title: Discovery
history.detail: Bayer–Onyx RAF inhibitor programme identifies BAY 43-9006.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Nexavar for advanced renal cell carcinoma.

history.title: Liver cancer
history.detail: SHARP shows a survival gain in advanced HCC; FDA approval follows (NEJM 2008).

history.title: Indian compulsory licence
history.detail: India grants Natco Pharma its first compulsory licence to make generic sorafenib at a fraction of the brand price.

history.title: Thyroid cancer
history.detail: Approval for radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (DECISION); Amgen acquires Onyx.

history.title: Superseded in HCC
history.detail: IMbrave150 shows atezolizumab plus bevacizumab outperforms sorafenib first-line in HCC.

pk.metabolism: hepatic CYP3A4 oxidation and UGT1A9 glucuronidation

facts: The 2012 Indian compulsory licence cut the monthly cost from about 280,000 rupees to about 8,800 rupees.
